parsed.explanation: This is a national-plus-state combined regime in which the sharpest traveller exposure is documentary: sex-assigned-at-birth passports, refusal where a discrepancy casts doubt on sex, and a possible lifetime fraud ineligibility finding, with documented confiscations, stranding and detentions of foreign citizens. Facilities access is restricted nationally and, in this state, a misdemeanour attaches to trans use of public changing facilities where a minor is present. If detention follows, the documented custody record is severe (forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse, conversion practices). Offsetting: no criminalisation of trans identity as such, a national gender-identity hate-crime statute, courts enjoining several measures, and legal-aid guidance. Weighted, this sits below the refused-entry-no-detention anchors and above the arbitrary-extortion anchors.

entry_documents.exposure: National policy requires sex assigned at birth on documents; X markers ended for new issues. Posts must refuse cases where a document discrepancy or reasonable doubt about sex exists, and may pursue a material-misrepresentation finding supporting permanent lifetime ineligibility. Passports confiscated/blocked; travellers stranded; detentions of neighbouring-state citizens documented.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiry; foreign ministry's 1992 policy was superseded only in November 2025 and remains under challenge; legal-aid FAQ on document rules exists.
entry_documents.interaction: A visitor's home-issued marker meets a national adjudication regime that treats mismatch as a screening trigger; once flagged, the case moves from border questioning into immigration fraud analysis and possible removal/refusal.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody documented as abusive for trans detainees: forced labour with guards' gendered taunts, beatings, solitary confinement, severe sexual abuse. National corrections bureau adopted a state model imposing conversion-style practices (hair cutting, hormone removal, psychiatric substitution); trans prisoner counts no longer reported.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; some executive orders enjoined in court; limited waiver possibilities on fraud findings.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry-stage document doubt can convert a visitor into a detainee, at which point custody placement by birth sex and the documented abuse record govern; consular access is not described.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: This state's Act 619 makes trans use of public restrooms, locker rooms or changing facilities a misdemeanour where a minor is present and intent to arouse/gratify is shown, and bars K-12 facility use by gender identity (extended 2025). Nationally, bans cover all government buildings in 10 jurisdictions; 4 make bathroom use criminal in some circumstances.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Act 619's trespass analogue requires refusal to depart, not automatic arrest; some states have no ban. No state-level protection here.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visitor using a public facility with a child present falls under state criminal law independent of the national entry regime; enforcement record under Act 619 is undocumented, but one arrest elsewhere under a similar law is recorded.

care_services.exposure: State law lets practitioners cite religious belief to deny LGBT patients care; 2021 minor care ban is enforced after the August 2025 appellate reversal, with litigation continuing. National measures target gender-affirming care funding and records.
care_services.protection: National judge previously enjoined the state ban for irreparable harm; injunction later reversed. Emergency-care obligations not documented.
care_services.interaction: An adult visitor needing routine or emergency care may face religious-objection refusal at state level; minors' care is directly restricted.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: May 2026 national counterterrorism strategy prioritises neutralising groups described as 'radically pro-transgender'; a DOJ reward memorandum uses 'radical gender ideology' as an extremist viewpoint. Public opinion: 66% back birth-sex document laws.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Same strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; the phrase is not a reward criterion.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Frames trans advocacy as a security-relevant category, raising the chance that visible trans status or activism draws investigative attention layered onto border screening.

minors_guardians.exposure: State bans gender-affirming care for under-18s (enforced since August 2025); K-12 facility restriction; school sports ban with private right to sue; national order directs investigation and prosecution of teachers who affirm a trans minor. Act 619 attaches where a minor is present.
minors_guardians.protection: Care-ban litigation continues; some national orders enjoined.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian travelling with a trans minor faces facility and care restrictions at state level, and any documentation mismatch at the border escalates for the whole family unit.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence statistics or pattern documented; travel guide notes safety varies by state. State has no hate-crime enhancement and its civil intimidation remedy excludes gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity since 2009.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Street-level risk is undocumented; if violence occurs, the state-level remedy is thin and only national statute applies.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Oversight is partial: courts have enjoined several orders but allowed passport restrictions; state-level protections absent; enforcement of Act 619 undocumented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties litigation ongoing; injunctions granted in several matters; national hate-crime coverage; legal-aid FAQ.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse exists but is slow and uneven; it has not changed the operative document regime, so it discounts rather than removes the entry exposure.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A is refusal of entry with document confiscation and no detention. Here refusal is compounded by a possible lifetime fraud ineligibility finding, documented detentions of foreign citizens over identity/visa issues, and a state criminal facility provision — so this case sits materially lower.

0.25-A is arbitrary detention, mockery and cash extortion without legal framework. This dossier has comparable documented custody severity but a systematic legal regime rather than ad hoc extortion, plus some working injunctions and a national hate-crime statute — slightly above 0.25, not a tier higher.

0.55-B involves delay, a notarised letter and eventual clearance with no detention. Here the operative rules themselves direct refusal and fraud analysis on discrepancy, and facility law carries criminal exposure, so this case is clearly lower.

parsed.synthesis: The visitor's dominant exposure is documentary and state-imposed: a home passport that does not match presentation triggers mandatory doubt-based refusal analysis and possible permanent ineligibility, with documented confiscations and detentions. If screening converts to detention, the custody record is severe. Layered on top, this state criminalises trans use of changing facilities where a minor is present and bars K-12 facility access. Working courts, a national hate-crime statute and ongoing litigation discount but do not remove these exposures, since the passport regime was allowed to take effect and facility law remains on the books.
